clue.text: In the evening eat up about a pound extra

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other here
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper, the evening meal
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone eats an evening meal costing about a pound extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SUP into PUS, which goes 'about' L.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus means in addition, as in a bonus plus expenses.

clue.text: The tedious guy must be tolerated

definitions.meaning: a dull person who wearies everyone
past tense of bear, to put up with

explanation.surface: A dull fellow simply has to be put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull person is a bore, and someone who put up with something bore it.

clue.text: The very best fruit

definitions.meaning: a stone fruit from the orchard

explanation.surface: The finest fruit of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum means the choicest pick, as in a plum role, and is also a purple stone fruit.

clue.text: No ridge can be overlooked

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: No hilltop ridge may be left unnoticed by the walker.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to pay it no attention, to disregard it.

clue.text: The delinquent yet manly element

parts.note: manly is a sense of male, masculine
a factor is a contributing element

explanation.surface: A young offender who is nevertheless rather masculine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or criminal is called a malefactor.

clue.text: Underwater illumination?

parts.note: read playfully, a light submerged by a flood; really a powerful lamp lighting a stadium or building

explanation.definitionFit: A strong lamp beam flooding a wide area with light, used for sports grounds and buildings.

clue.text: Salvage collector in Gateshead walking unsteadily

parts.note: a totter is a rag-and-bone man who collects scrap
read as Gates' head, the first letter of Gates

explanation.surface: A scrap dealer in a northern English town staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; read as 'Gates head' it gives G. A totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottering is moving with a shaky, swaying gait.

clue.text: Drink cocktail, looking wooden

parts.note: tea is a common drink
read as cock's tail, the last letter of cock

explanation.surface: Someone sipping a cocktail looks stiff and expressionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hardwood timber, so a teak table is a wooden one.

clue.text: The new entrant is only temporary

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The latest newcomer is just passing through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient is fleeting, lasting a short while.

clue.text: Met a sabot maker demonstrating craft

indicators.note: maker suggests the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone meets a clog maker showing off their handiwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam-powered vessel is a kind of watercraft.

clue.text: Copy an article on exercise

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Copy out an article about exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to mimic or imitate.

clue.text: A page no longer gets a tip

parts.note: an ex is a former, no longer current, partner

explanation.surface: A page boy no longer in service receives a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the topmost point or peak of something.

clue.text: A little joint to roast a nice golden brown

indicators.note: a little of these words means only a small run of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A small joint is roasted to a fine golden colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tan is a light yellowish-brown colour, as of sunburnt skin.

clue.text: Watch pet mice scampering about-that's the answer

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other
scampering mice dart about, so their letters run into a new order

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Pet mice run about the clock face: problem solved!
explanation.walkthrough: 'scampering' turns PET MICE into TIMEPCE, which goes 'about' IE. 'the answer' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a small portable timekeeping device.

clue.text: Traded in smaller model

indicators.note: in places one word within the other

parts.note: tinier means smaller
sold means traded away

explanation.surface: Something exchanged for a smaller replica.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy soldier cast in metal is a small model figure.

clue.text: Works to produce a feature with little hesitation in May

indicators.note: in places these pieces within the name of the month

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A factory makes a product with barely a pause in the spring month.
explanation.definitionFit: The works of a machine, its moving parts, are its machinery.

clue.text: Drive all the way

parts.note: to push something firmly to its conclusion, as with an attack or argument

explanation.definitionFit: To press home an advantage is to drive it through to the end.

clue.text: Pause for a bracer

definitions.meaning: to halt or remain for a while
a support or prop, like a rope bracing a mast

explanation.surface: Stop for a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to linger or pause, and a stay is a rope or prop that braces a mast.

clue.text: Sought admittance, but was not at all appreciative

definitions.meaning: rapped on the door to be let in

explanation.surface: A visitor asked to be let in but was very rude about the welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: One raps on a door to be let in, and to criticise something harshly is to run it down.

clue.text: The mountain nymph, sweet Milton (L Allegro)

definitions.text: The mountain nymph, sweet Milton (L Allegro)

parts.words: The mountain nymph, sweet Milton (L Allegro)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the line from John Milton's poem L'Allegro naming the mountain nymph

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's L'Allegro has the line 'The mountain nymph, sweet ...', personifying freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton personifies freedom as a mountain nymph in his poem.

clue.text: Prison-officers require the use of drawers

indicators.note: making use of the letters means rearranging them into a new word

explanation.surface: Jail guards need chests of drawers for their uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, a warder is a guard in a prison.

clue.text: An American Indian would have to dance before one

indicators.note: before places the dance ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Native American is obliged to dance in front of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of northeastern Arizona.

clue.text: Real thugs can make a killing!

indicators.note: can make suggests these letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Genuine gangsters can earn huge sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughter is a brutal killing, often of many.

clue.text: The man over fifty was once revered in Scandinavia

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: he refers to a man
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An older man of fifty used to be honoured up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Hel was the goddess of the underworld worshipped in old Norse religion.

clue.text: Sort of theatre that lacks aspiration?

parts.note: lacking means having no
an aspirate is a breathed h sound

explanation.surface: A kind of theatre with no ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition but is the sounded H.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh is a classical Japanese masked drama.

clue.text: Move slowly, causing some irritation

definitions.meaning: a sharpness or touch of irritability, as in a voice

explanation.surface: Creeping along is bound to annoy people.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward bit by bit is to edge, and a voice with sharpness has an edge to it.

clue.text: A member of the fraternity, though not even a don

parts.note: odd numbers are not even
a fellow is a senior member of a college, a don

explanation.surface: A brother who is a strange college academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a British friendly society, a fraternal order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oddfellows are a fraternal friendly society with lodges and members.

clue.text: Some speech or other that evokes memories

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A talk or two that brings back old times.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder or reflection of the past is an echo of it.

clue.text: Bound to provide grassland parking

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Sure to offer meadow parking for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a jump or spring.

clue.text: Ford put certain points about publicity

indicators.note: about places these points round the next piece

parts.note: W and E are compass points, west and east
an ad is publicity for a product

explanation.surface: A car maker's name placed beside promotional material.
explanation.definitionFit: To ford a river is to cross it on foot through shallow water.

clue.text: Trust looking for the right place in the Fens

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
Ely is a cathedral city in the Fens of Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Faith seeking the proper spot in the flat East Anglian marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low marshy lands in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to depend on them.

clue.text: Down to the ground

parts.note: heading downwards towards the planet's surface

explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards the planet's surface, downwards.
